scope: PERF.1b: native non-SHA qualification; conditional bulk backend candidate only after same-runner micro evidence. Preserve current SHA-NI behavior.
runner_delta: Same CPU model/kernel/XFS and no SHA feature; now 2 visible CPUs and 8 GiB rather than earlier 1 CPU/2 GiB. No historical timing ratios.
build_execution: Both binaries built on development host with identical compiler/flags/dependencies; frozen hashes/source manifests copied to runner. Native execution, not emulation. No remote compiler installation.
micro_groups: Existing eight groups plus 512 MiB dense and sparse-pattern groups (1 MiB chunks); ordinary caches, no cold claim.
repeat_policy: Every group gets all repeats, irrespective of sign. Retain failed runs, adverse observations and timing spreads.
candidate_gate: Require bulk micro benefit on non-SHA CPU before testing a private runtime-selected retained payload backend. Hardware SHA-capable x86-64 uses existing sha2; preserve other architecture defaults.
workflow_gate: Frozen native normal/reconciliation/attestation/acknowledgment and direct/whole-CLI controls on runner XFS/private tmpfs and development Btrfs/private tmpfs. Same filesystems/caches/affinity/verification per pair. All groups 3x4+3x8 pairs.
correctness: Known vectors and independent dense/sparse digests; candidate full workspace and real CLI fixture tests, existing fault/process-loss/cancellation/identity/sparse/durability checks.
resources: CPU0 affinity; one measured workload per host; builds/tests/plots never concurrent with that host timing. Separate hosts may execute independent work concurrently; no cross-host timing ratio.
promotion: Accept only bounded same-runner benefit with SHA-NI regression controls; otherwise retain baseline and commit diagnostics.
privacy: Authored synthetic fixtures on existing guest only. No ESXi operation, exports, VM resource modification or credentials in public evidence.
